title: The first crisp morning, Saturday 8am, 48 degrees
moment: It is the first crisp day of fall, Saturday, 8am, 48 degrees, and I am out on the walk with the second cup. The sun is still low and gold, coming in from the right over the roofline, so the whole street is shade with one band of light laid across it, and the wet leaves on the sidewalk hold that band back up at me in broken pieces. I have a grey cotton sweatshirt on with the sleeves pulled over my hands, and the coffee steam is visible for the first time this year, standing straight up and then crossing the light. Everything is sharper than it was in August: the edges of the roofline, the cold on the back of my neck, the click of the pen clipped to the pocket notebook in my other hand. Nothing is moving except the steam and me.

light.source: the low sun itself, no diffusion, clearing the roofline to the right of the frame
light.fill: a low broken band of small wet mirrored patches on the walk, throwing the key back up into the underside of the subject at 3200K, dim and fragmented

objects: wet concrete walk in shade, dark grey with a cold cast
the one gold band the low sun lays across that wet concrete
a heather grey cotton fleece cuff pulled over the knuckles
black coffee in a plain grey cup
steam standing straight up off the cup and crossing the light
the grey board cover of a pocket book, dry paper
the brushed steel clip of a pen on that cover
the cold blue of the sky above the roofline, unlit

inventory.gaze: out along the walk, level with the street

inventory.keepsake: the one gold band of light across the wet walk, everything else in shade
inventory.utterance: We can see all the way to the corner today.
